html:
A great earthquake that struck the coast of Peru on the night of 28 October 1746, among the strongest known in the region. Its estimated magnitude was about 8.6 to 8.8.

Most of Lima, capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru, was knocked down: houses, churches and much of the cathedral. Then a tsunami struck the port of Callao and almost wiped it out, sweeping ships inland. Of Callao's several thousand people, only a few hundred are said to have survived. In all, thousands died.

The viceroy, José Manso de Velasco, led the rebuilding and was made Count of Superunda ("over the waves") for it. He wanted lower buildings and wider streets, but the church and the rich resisted. Lima was rebuilt with lighter upper floors of cane and plaster, and wooden balconies that became part of its look. Like the Lisbon earthquake nine years later, the disaster made people argue over God, nature and the planning of cities.
sum: A great earthquake that struck the coast of Peru on the night of 28 October 1746, among the strongest known in the region. Its estimated magnitude was about 8.6 to 8.8.
